record.paper_title: Local and Global Methods in Data Mining: Basic Techniques and Open Problems
record.original_question: Given a hypergraph, a transversal is a minimal set of vertices that intersects every edge. Is there an algorithm that enumerates all transversals in time polynomial in the combined size of the input hypergraph and the output list of transversals?

evidence.quote: Problem 13 Find a polynomial time algorithm (in the size of the input and output) for enumerating all transversals.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let H = (V, E) be a finite hypergraph, where V is a finite set of vertices and E is a finite collection of subsets of V (the edges). A transversal (or minimal hitting set) of H is a subset T ⊆ V such that T ∩ e ≠ ∅ for every edge e ∈ E, and no proper subset of T has this property. Let Tr(H) denote the family of all transversals of H.

Question: Does there exist an algorithm that, on input H, outputs every element of Tr(H) (each exactly once) and runs in time bounded by a polynomial in |H| + |Tr(H)|, where |H| denotes the encoding size of the hypergraph and |Tr(H)| denotes the total encoding size of the list of all transversals?
artifact.status_search_result: The existence of an output-polynomial algorithm for enumerating all minimal transversals of a hypergraph remains a major open problem in algorithmic enumeration, open for over 25 years. The best known algorithm, due to Fredman and Khachiyan (1996), runs in incremental quasi-polynomial time N^{O(log N / log log N)}, where N is the combined input/output size. Polynomial-time algorithms are known only in restricted cases (e.g., bounded degeneracy/dimension, certain structural classes), but the general question is unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Hypergraph dualization with FPT-delay parameterized by the degeneracy and dimension
status_evidence.snippet: It is the major open question in enumeration, whether the transversal hypergraph problem can be solved in output-polynomial time.
status_evidence.claim: The general problem is still open.

status_evidence.title: Efficiently Enumerating Hitting Sets of Hypergraphs Arising in Data Profiling
status_evidence.snippet: The currently fastest algorithm was presented by Fredman and Khachiyan and runs in time N^{O(log N / log log N)}.
status_evidence.claim: Best known bound is quasi-polynomial, not polynomial.
